title: Flannery O'Connor's birth chart
metaDescription: Flannery O'Connor's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 4.5° Aries. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Sun stands at 4.5° Aries, in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun sits at 4.5° Aries — the first decan, 0°–10°, which the tradition sub-rules by Mars. Degrees matter more than the sign label here: two people born a fortnight apart share Aries and share almost nothing else about where the Sun actually stood.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Aries (22.0°), Venus in Pisces (27.0°), Mars in Gemini (1.1°): a mind that decides at speaking speed, taste tuned to mood and undertow, drive that argues its way forward.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The day's firmest angle joins Mercury and Neptune — a trine holding at 1.9°. A third of the circle is the tradition’s friendliest distance — same element, shared assumptions, no translation required. Behind it, Saturn trine Pluto at 2.1°, and Mercury square Jupiter at 2.6° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The day-stable angles form no closed figure. Nothing funnels; each aspect is its own negotiation, which the tradition reads as a chart of separate treaties rather than one campaign.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Three planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. The Sun in Aries at 4.5° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Venus in Pisces at 27.0° is in exaltation; Jupiter in Capricorn at 19.4° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given. None of these labels is a verdict on a person; they describe how a function is situated, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The honest balance sheet uses the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: fire 4, water 4, air 1, earth 1 across the elements, and cardinal 5, mutable 3, fixed 2 across the modalities. Saturn and Neptune were retrograde. Pluto changed direction during the day, so its motion is left open.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Aries for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.4° between midnight and midnight. The missing clock moves the Moon by half a sign at most here, and the boundary was never close. At the noon reference it stands at 18.6°.
